text:
lara: Heads-up — hit a KV cache OOM on p3-high during a traffic spike. Patterns: lots of long contexts (~4k tokens) + large gen budgets. Batch formation coalesced several heavy-KV requests and blew past expected allocations.

sam: Which pool/trace? Any quick repro?

lara: Trace uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/kvcache/1769007650.tar.gz. Pool: p3-high. Kernel path observed: aten_fused_attention_v2 (we fell back there for int8 model).

mohit: I think the recent bump to max_tokens_per_batch to 40k allowed too many large-ctx requests to aggregate. We need memory-aware batching not just token-count.

ying: Agreed. We should estimate kv_size(request) = ctx_len * kv_slot_size * hidden_width_factor. We already know ctx_len per request. Add a kv_budget check during queueing.

paul: Proposal: maintain running kv_bytes_in_flight per-worker. When forming a batch, ensure kv_bytes_in_flight + sum(kv_estimates) < soft_kv_limit (e.g., 0.85 * GPU_MEM). If over, split or demote low-priority reqs to streaming/fastpath.

lara: Also observed a small perf regression after kernel-intro changes: kernel selection sometimes picks a slower, higher-memory kernel under pressure. We should bias selection toward memory-frugal kernels when kv_budget is low.

sam: Quick pseudo patch idea: 
```
# batcher pseudo
for req in queue:
  estimate = kv_estimate(req)
  if current_kv_bytes + estimate > soft_limit:
     if req.priority == low:
         route_to_streaming(req)
     else:
         cut_generation_budget(req, target_tokens = min(req.gen_budget, fallback_budget_per_ctx))
  else:
     include_in_batch(req)
```
This lets us avoid OOMs by either splitting work or trimming budgets.

mohit: Two caveats: (1) many small requests can still cause KV churn due to allocator fragmentation, (2) we need an eviction/flush policy for low-reuse prefixes. Consider epoch-based LRU or proactive KV compaction.

ying: Also tie kernel selection to kv state: kernel_score = latency_ms + lambda * kv_bytes_used. When kv_bytes_used high, prefer kernels with lower kv footprint even if slightly slower. Add this to compile/kernel-picker.

paul: I'll run a 24h replay in perf-test with soft_limit=0.8*mem and the new scheduler heuristics, compare OOM rate, p50/p99 latencies, and token throughput.

lara: Add metrics before canary: kv_bytes_in_flight (gauge), kv-rejects (counter), batch-splits (counter). Alert if kv-rejects > 0.1% of requests in 5m window.

sam: I'll open a PR with: queue-level kv check + metrics + feature flag to enable memory-aware batching. Target canary on dedicated pool next week.

mohit: Also ensure we have a hot fallback: kernel that spills KV to CPU-pinned buffers when GPU alloc fails. That saved us last time — surface it in scheduler.

ying: I'll add a synthetic stress test in perf repo that simulates mixed ctx/generation distributions and asserts no OOM across 10k requests.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: pr/5423 -> canary/dedicated at 2026-03-20 05:00 UTC

paul: Nice. Follow-ups: sam -> PR, ying -> perf tests, mohit -> KV fragmentation investigation, lara -> dashboard + alerts.

lara: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
